text: Morphology [Gr. morfh , form]: Ger. Morphologie ; Fr. morphologie ; Ital. morfologia . The philosophical study of comparative anatomy, being chiefly concerned with the genesis and homology of the structure and parts of living organisms. First used by Goethe, in 1817, to denote the study of form. Literature : HAECKEL, Gen. Morphologie (1868); CARUS, Gesch. d. Zool.; art. 'Morphology' in Encyc. Brit. (9th ed.). ( E.S.G. )
